citation: Servin M., Vesterlund F., Wallin E. (2021) Digital twins with distributed particle simulation for mine-to-mill material tracking. arXiv:2104.09111

dedupe_keys.name: particle based digital twin for mine to mill material tracking servin vesterlund and wallin

description: This model represents ore in a mining operation as pseudo-particles, each standing for a large collection of real particles of various sizes, shapes and mineral properties, and moves them through the chain of transport and processing from mine to mill. Movements and changes of state are driven by combined data from control systems, sensors, vehicle telematics and simulation models where no real sensors can see, and each digital particle carries observations made by equipment as it handles the material, so that material properties can be learned from process data and effects on downstream processes predicted. It was developed by Martin Servin, Folke Vesterlund and Erik Wallin and posted on arXiv on 19 April 2021 as a 19-page paper, tested on a mining simulator. It applies to individual mine sites. The preprint is available free online as a PDF; no code or licence is given on the abstract page. Caveats: the method was demonstrated on a simulator, not a working mine, and it needs rich data from equipment and telematics. For simulation it shows how digital twins can follow material through mining supply chains, supporting optimisation of haulage, stockpiles and processing and analysis of how disruptions at one stage propagate downstream. It is related to the Eclipse Ditto record in this catalogue, a framework for keeping digital twins in sync with devices.
